grades.label: Admission, Program Declaration, and Continuation
grades.text: To continue in the program, students must maintain a 2.25 cumulative grade point average (CGPA)*.

grades.label: Admission, Program Declaration, and Continuation
grades.text: Students whose CGPA falls below 2.25 cannot enroll in any upper division CRIM courses.

grades.label: Admission, Program Declaration, and Continuation
grades.text: *transfer students who meet the criminology program declaration requirements upon admission to SFU may use their admission CGPA for declaration purposes

grades.label: Upper Division Course Access
grades.text: Students with a minimum 2.25 CGPA are eligible to enroll in upper division criminology courses upon successful completion of 45 units and certificate declaration.

grades.label: Graduation Requirements
grades.text: In addition to normal university grade point average requirements, the School of Criminology requires the following: for graduation, students must obtain a minimum 2.25 CGPA, 2.25 UDGPA, 2.25 criminology course CGPA (calculated on all CRIM courses completed at SFU), and 2.25 criminology course UDGPA (calculated on all upper division CRIM courses completed at SFU).
